enzyme_name: Branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase (3alpha,7alpha,12alpha-trihydroxy-5beta-cholestanoyl-CoA oxidase), ACOX2
organism_context: Mammalian peroxisome (human, rat); 24,25-desaturation step of primary bile acid synthesis. KEGG only offers the generic ortholog K00257 (acyl-ACP/acyl-CoA dehydrogenase) for R04592.
rationale: The THCA-CoA desaturation in peroxisomal bile acid synthesis is run by ACOX2, a single-activity FAD acyl-CoA oxidase; the bifunctional enzyme of this pathway is the next one in line (D-bifunctional protein / HSD17B4), not this one.
direction_note: An acyl-CoA oxidase reoxidises its flavin with O2 to H2O2 (a dehydrogenase would use ETF); writing free FAD/FADH2 as the couple removes exactly the step that makes desaturation irreversible, and physiological flux is THCA-CoA -> 24-ene-CoA, the LLM direction.

enzyme_name: beta-Glucosidase (beta-D-glucosyl-2-coumarinate glucohydrolase)
organism_context: Plants - Melilotus alba (sweet clover) coumarin pathway, B-gene beta-glucosidase; family GH1 glycoside hydrolases generally.
rationale: GH1 beta-glucosidases carry one glycoside-hydrolase activity; the Melilotus enzyme releases free 2-coumarate from the stored glucoside on tissue disruption, after which the aglycone lactonises to coumarin.
direction_note: At cellular water activity a glycosidase only hydrolyses; ModelSEED's '<' would have the enzyme condense free glucose onto the aglycone, a reaction that in vivo requires UDP-glucose and a glucosyltransferase.

enzyme_name: beta-Glucosidase (beta-D-glucosyl-2-coumarinate glucohydrolase)
organism_context: Plants - Melilotus alba coumarin pathway; same KEGG entry (R04998) as rxn15505, duplicated here with the alpha-anomer of glucose.
rationale: Same single-activity GH1 beta-glucosidase as rxn15505; note that a retaining beta-glucosidase releases beta-D-glucose, so the alpha-D-glucose written here can only arise by subsequent mutarotation - this is an anomer-duplicate entry, not a second enzyme.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only direction a beta-glucosidase runs in vivo, so the LLM's '>' is the enzymologically supported side.

enzyme_name: none identified - KEGG R05840 carries no EC number, no ortholog and no enzyme
organism_context: KEGG vitamin B6 metabolism map (rn00750); a legacy sketch predating the two characterised B6 routes (DXP-dependent PdxA/PdxJ and DXP-independent PdxS/PdxT).
rationale: No enzyme is assigned to R05840 and the entry is not mass-balanced (C9H17NO7 in, C8H11NO3 out - roughly a CO2 and two waters missing), so it is a whole-pathway condensation sketch rather than one enzymatic step. Judgement from the KEGG entry itself plus the known B6 biosynthetic routes; no literature supports a single enzyme here.
direction_note: KEGG draws it inside the B6 biosynthesis map, i.e. toward pyridoxine (the LLM side), but with no enzyme and a broken mass balance neither arrow rests on enzymology.

enzyme_name: none identified - KEGG R05840 carries no EC number, no ortholog and no enzyme
organism_context: Same KEGG entry (R05840) as rxn15553, re-mapped here with D-alanine in place of L-alanine.
rationale: Identical non-enzymatic sketch to rxn15553, duplicated with the D-alanine stereoisomer; KEGG's own definition uses unspecified 'Alanine' (C01401), so the D/L split is a ModelSEED mapping artefact and no enzyme catalyses either version.
direction_note: Same as rxn15553: no enzyme, carbon count unbalanced, so the direction conflict is not resolvable from enzymology.

enzyme_name: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate synthase (PdxS/Pdx1 synthase subunit, acting with the PdxT/Pdx2 glutaminase subunit)
organism_context: Bacteria, archaea, fungi and plants using the DXP-independent B6 route (Bacillus subtilis, Geobacillus, Methanosarcina acetivorans, plant PDX1/PDX2).
rationale: PLP synthase is a 12-mer PdxS core decorated with 12 PdxT glutaminase subunits - two distinct polypeptides associating into a complex, not two catalytic domains on one chain - so by the protocol's complex exclusion the PdxS subunit that runs this ribulose-5-P/G3P condensation is monofunctional.
direction_note: KEGG R07456 also releases orthophosphate and 3 H2O, both dropped by ModelSEED; that phosphate release and ring aromatisation are what make PLP synthase irreversible in the biosynthetic (LLM) direction.

enzyme_name: Sterol C-22 desaturase (CYP61 / Erg5p), EC 1.14.19.41
organism_context: Fungi - Saccharomyces cerevisiae ERG5, Xanthophyllomyces dendrorhous; ergosterol biosynthesis (an unrelated non-P450 C-22 desaturase exists in Tetrahymena).
rationale: 5-Dehydroepisterol -> ergosta-5,7,22,24(28)-tetraenol is the C-22 desaturation of the ergosterol pathway, run by the single-activity microsomal cytochrome P450 Erg5/CYP61 (which works with a separate NADPH-P450 reductase, a partner protein rather than a fused domain).
direction_note: The real reaction is 5-dehydroepisterol + NADPH + H+ + O2 -> tetraenol + NADP+ + 2 H2O; with O2 deleted it reads as a reversible NADP+ dehydrogenation, which is what lets ModelSEED point it backwards.

enzyme_name: none identified - KEGG R07788 is flagged 'unclear reaction' with no EC and no ortholog
organism_context: Plants - Arabidopsis brassinosteroid pathway; both metabolites are substrates of the C-23 hydroxylases CYP90C1/CYP90D1 but no enzyme is known to interconvert them.
rationale: KEGG itself labels R07788 an 'unclear reaction'; Ohnishi et al. report 22alpha-hydroxy-5alpha-campestan-3-one and 3-epi-6-deoxocathasterone as parallel CYP90C1/D1 substrates feeding the C-23 hydroxylation shortcut, not as the product pair of a characterised 3-oxo/3-ol enzyme.
direction_note: Written as a bare 3-oxo/3alpha-ol interconversion with '2 H+' standing in for the NAD(P)H any such reduction would need, so neither arrow is enzymologically grounded.

enzyme_name: Steroid 5alpha-reductase DET2 (DEETIOLATED2; pea LK)
organism_context: Plants - Arabidopsis DET2, pea LK; the early C-22 oxidation branch of brassinosteroid biosynthesis.
rationale: Converting (22R,23R)-22,23-dihydroxy-campest-4-en-3-one to 3-dehydro-6-deoxoteasterone is a delta-4 5alpha-reduction, the DET2 steroid 5alpha-reductase step; DET2 is a single-activity NADPH-dependent reductase, and the C-23 hydroxylation that generates its substrate is done by the separate CYP90C1/D1 enzymes.
direction_note: NADPH is replaced by '2 H+', deleting the irreversibility of the 5alpha-reduction; KEGG additionally flags R07790 as an 'unclear reaction', so confidence in any direction call is limited.

enzyme_name: beta-Glucuronidase (luteolin triglucuronide beta-glucuronidase), EC 3.2.1.31
organism_context: Plants - rye (Secale cereale) mesophyll vacuole, where luteolin 7-O-diglucuronide-4'-O-glucuronide is the major leaf flavone (MetaCyc PWY-7445).
rationale: The activity is a vacuolar plant beta-glucuronidase that trims the 4'-glucuronide off luteolin triglucuronide; the protein has never been cloned, so the monofunctional call rests on the single-activity architecture of glucuronide-hydrolysing glycosidases rather than on a characterised sequence.
direction_note: ModelSEED's '<' would require glucuronide synthesis from free glucuronic acid; in vivo that needs UDP-glucuronate and a glucuronosyltransferase, so only the hydrolytic (LLM) direction is available to this enzyme.

enzyme_name: beta-Glucuronidase (bacterial GUS; human lysosomal GUSB), EC 3.2.1.31
organism_context: Human gut bacteria (E. coli and other Enterobacteriaceae/Firmicutes GUS enzymes) reactivating SN-38 from SN-38G in the intestinal lumen; also human lysosomal GUSB.
rationale: SN-38G hydrolysis is the textbook bacterial beta-glucuronidase reaction behind irinotecan gut toxicity; GUS is a homotetramer of identical single-activity subunits (oligomeric, which the protocol explicitly does not count as bifunctional).
direction_note: SN-38 glucuronidation is a host UGT/UDP-glucuronate reaction, not the reverse of this hydrolase, so ModelSEED's '<' is not a reaction the glucuronidase can run.

enzyme_name: Pyrrolidine ketide synthase (PYKS, type III PKS) followed by a non-enzymatic Mannich condensation/decarboxylation
organism_context: Solanaceae (Atropa belladonna, Datura, Anisodus) and Erythroxylum; tropane/pyrrolidine alkaloid biosynthesis.
rationale: KEGG labels R08428 'multi-step reaction' and 'incomplete reaction': PYKS performs a single malonyl-CoA condensation to a 3-oxoglutaric acid intermediate which then condenses with N-methylpyrrolinium non-enzymatically, so no single enzyme converts methylpyrrolinium to hygrine.
direction_note: The two malonyl-CoA units supplying hygrine's extra carbons are absent from the equation; pathway flux does run toward hygrine (the LLM side), but through a partly spontaneous multi-step route rather than a reversible enzyme.

enzyme_name: none - superseded futalosine-pathway entry; the real first step is MqnA chorismate dehydratase (chorismate -> 3-[(1-carboxyvinyl)oxy]benzoate)
organism_context: Bacteria with the futalosine menaquinone pathway (Streptomyces, Thermus, Helicobacter pylori, Campylobacter jejuni, Chlamydia).
rationale: KEGG has deleted R08586 (rest.kegg.jp and the KEGG entry page both return 'no such data'); the originally proposed chorismate -> futalosine step was replaced by MqnA (chorismate dehydratase), then MqnE and MqnB, and the real intermediate is aminodeoxyfutalosine, so no enzyme catalyses this lumped conversion.
direction_note: The inosine/adenosine co-substrate is missing and KEGG no longer carries the entry; menaquinone biosynthesis nevertheless flows chorismate -> futalosine-type intermediates, i.e. the LLM direction, never back to chorismate.

enzyme_name: MqnD, 5,8-dihydroxy-2-naphthoate synthase (cyclic dehypoxanthine futalosine lyase), EC 4.1.99.29
organism_context: Futalosine-pathway bacteria (Thermus thermophilus, Streptomyces coelicolor, Helicobacter pylori). Note KEGG's '1,4-dihydroxy-6-naphthoate' is the old name for 5,8-dihydroxy-2-naphthoate.
rationale: MqnD is a single-activity lyase that opens cyclic dehypoxanthine futalosine by hemiacetal ring opening, tautomerisation and retro-aldol cleavage, releasing the dihydroxynaphthoate plus dihydroxyacetone; the EC 1.14.-.- on the ModelSEED record is wrong (no oxygenase is involved).
direction_note: The co-product glycerone (dihydroxyacetone) is missing from the ModelSEED equation; releasing that fragment by retro-aldol is precisely what makes the step unidirectional in the biosynthetic (LLM) direction.

enzyme_name: none identified - KEGG deleted R08598 and now splits the conversion across a 3-ketoreductase and the 3,5-epimerase (R08597)
organism_context: Actinomycete polyketide 2,6-dideoxysugar biosynthesis (dTDP-L-olivose / dTDP-L-oleandrose modules, KEGG M00799/M00801).
rationale: R08598 returns 404 from KEGG; current KEGG routes dTDP-2,6-dideoxy-L-glycero-hex-2-enos-4-ulose (C11931) to dTDP-4-oxo-2,6-dideoxy-L-mannose (C11927) via R08591, a 3-ketoreduction and the 3,5-epimerase R08597, so at least two enzymes and an NAD(P)H are hidden inside this single ModelSEED entry.
direction_note: NAD(P)H is written as a bare '2 H+'; the dTDP-sugar pathway nonetheless runs only toward the 2,6-dideoxy sugar for glycosylation of the polyketide, i.e. the LLM direction.

enzyme_name: unassigned - EC 1.13.11.18 (persulfide/sulfur dioxygenase, ETHE1 / SdoA family) is attached but does not catalyse the equation as written
organism_context: Mitochondrial ETHE1 in animals and plants; bacterial persulfide dioxygenases (Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acidithiobacillus) in sulfide/sulfur oxidation.
rationale: KEGG has deleted R08677 (404), and the enzyme named by EC 1.13.11.18 actually oxidises glutathione persulfide with O2 and water to sulfite + GSH; the equation here (GSH + S0 <=> GSSH) is a non-oxidative sulfane transfer that a rhodanese-type sulfurtransferase or plain solution chemistry performs, so the labelled enzyme and the written reaction do not match.
direction_note: As written this is a sulfane-sulfur exchange whose direction follows the GSH/GSSH/S0 pools; the O2 and sulfite that make the genuine sulfur-dioxygenase reaction irreversible are nowhere in the equation.

enzyme_name: Coclaurine N-methyltransferase (CNMT), EC 2.1.1.115
organism_context: Benzylisoquinoline alkaloid plants - Coptis japonica, Papaver somniferum, Thalictrum flavum.
rationale: CNMT is a single-activity SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase; its crystal structure shows one methyl-transfer active site with broad substrate tolerance (which is promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity).
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible in the methylating direction, so ModelSEED's '<' would require N-demethylation with SAM regeneration, which this enzyme cannot do.

enzyme_name: Deamino-alpha-keto-demethylphosphinothricin aminotransferase (uncharacterised PLP aminotransferase of the bialaphos/phosalacine cluster)
organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus / S. viridochromogenes bialaphos and Kitasatospora phosalacine pathways.
rationale: KEGG annotates R08877 only with the free-text comment 'aminotransferase' and assigns no EC, gene or ortholog; the specific transaminase for this step of the phosphinothricin pathway has not been characterised, so the enzyme cannot be classified honestly.
direction_note: The amino donor/acceptor pair (glutamate/2-oxoglutarate) is missing entirely, and transaminases are freely reversible with direction set by amino-donor pools - though pathway flux runs keto acid -> demethylphosphinothricin, i.e. opposite to ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: none - lumped TCA-like chain-extension segment (FrbC 2-phosphonomethylmalate synthase, an aconitase-like isomerase and an oxidative decarboxylase)
organism_context: Streptomyces rubellomurinus FR-900098 biosynthesis (and the related fosmidomycin cluster in S. lavendulae).
rationale: KEGG's own comment on R08881 is 'multi-step reaction (similar to TCA cycle, R01325+R01900+R00709...)': the one-carbon chain extension takes a homocitrate-synthase-like condensation with acetyl-CoA (FrbC), an aconitase-like isomerisation and an NAD-dependent oxidative decarboxylation, so no single enzyme catalyses it.
direction_note: ModelSEED still carries the superseded KEGG substrate (cpd01807 = C02798, 3-phosphonopyruvate) where current KEGG R08881 reads (R)-2-(phosphonomethyl)malate; either way the acetyl-CoA condensation plus CO2 release make the segment unidirectional toward the phosphonate, the LLM side.

enzyme_name: none - lumped FR-900098 tailoring segment (transamination/decarboxylation plus FrbG N-hydroxylation and FrbF N-acetylation on a cytidylylated carrier)
organism_context: Streptomyces rubellomurinus FR-900098 (antimalarial phosphonate) biosynthesis.
rationale: KEGG labels R08882 both 'multi-step reaction' and 'incomplete reaction'; converting 2-oxo-4-phosphonobutanoate to FR-900098 needs decarboxylation/transamination followed by N-hydroxylation and N-acetylation carried out by separate Frb proteins, so there is no single catalysing enzyme.
direction_note: A dedicated secondary-metabolite assembly line runs only toward its product; ModelSEED's '<' would mean FR-900098 catabolism, which this cluster does not perform.

enzyme_name: none - lumped rhizocticin assembly line (phosphonoacetaldehyde aldol condensation, transamination/dehydration to the APPA residue, then ATP-dependent peptide ligation)
organism_context: Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 rhi gene cluster; phosphono-oligopeptide antifungals (rhizocticins A-D).
rationale: KEGG labels R08883 a 'multi-step reaction': phosphonoacetaldehyde is elaborated to the (Z)-2-amino-5-phosphono-3-pentenoate (APPA) residue and then ligated into a di-/tripeptide by cluster-encoded ligases, so the entry collapses an entire pathway into one reaction with no catalysing enzyme.
direction_note: Only the phosphonate fragment appears on the left of a whole peptide on the right, so the equation is badly unbalanced; ATP-driven peptide assembly is unidirectional toward rhizocticin, the LLM side.

enzyme_name: none - lumped rhizocticin assembly line (APPA formation from phosphonoacetaldehyde plus peptide ligation)
organism_context: Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 rhi cluster; rhizocticin A (Arg-APPA dipeptide).
rationale: Same KEGG 'multi-step reaction' lump as R08883, here producing rhizocticin A; several distinct enzymes (aldolase, aminotransferase/dehydratase, peptide ligases) lie between phosphonoacetaldehyde and the finished peptide.
direction_note: The amino-acid partners of the peptide are absent from the equation; biosynthesis of a secreted antibiotic runs only toward the product, the LLM side.

enzyme_name: none - lumped rhizocticin assembly line (APPA formation from phosphonoacetaldehyde plus peptide ligation)
organism_context: Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 rhi cluster; rhizocticin C.
rationale: Same KEGG 'multi-step reaction' lump as R08883/R08884, here producing rhizocticin C; no single enzyme converts phosphonoacetaldehyde into a finished phosphono-oligopeptide.
direction_note: Peptide amino-acid substrates and ATP are missing; the assembly line is unidirectional toward rhizocticin, the LLM side.

enzyme_name: none - lumped rhizocticin assembly line (APPA formation from phosphonoacetaldehyde plus peptide ligation)
organism_context: Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 rhi cluster; rhizocticin D.
rationale: Same KEGG 'multi-step reaction' lump as the other rhizocticin entries, here producing rhizocticin D; the conversion spans an aldol condensation, transamination/dehydration and ATP-dependent peptide ligation.
direction_note: Peptide amino-acid substrates and ATP are missing; the assembly line is unidirectional toward rhizocticin, the LLM side.

enzyme_name: none - lumped isomerisation plus oxidative decarboxylation of the bialaphos pathway (aconitase-like and isocitrate-dehydrogenase-like steps)
organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus / S. viridochromogenes bialaphos and phosalacine biosynthesis.
rationale: KEGG's comments on R08888 are explicit: 'multi-step reaction (similar to R01899+R00268)', 'enzyme not yet characterized', 'incomplete reaction' - 2-phosphinomethylmalate reaches the keto acid via an aconitase-like isomerisation then an NAD-dependent oxidative decarboxylation, so there is no single enzyme.
direction_note: The CO2 and NAD(H) of the oxidative decarboxylation are absent from the equation; that decarboxylation makes the segment unidirectional toward the keto acid, the LLM side, and against ModelSEED's '<'.
